translation: [Note] The classic says: One who has lost blood has no sweat, and one who has lost sweat has no blood. Both should have a pulse that is floating, faint, and rough. Now, when one examines it and it is so, this is a sign of exhaustion, and there is no sign of sweating; is it not lost blood? Therefore one knows there is a sign of lost blood from a metal wound or a blow or a fall. It is also discussed: When the liver pulse beats firm and the complexion does not change, there must have been a blow or a fall.
